title: Logical Operators
bullets: Combine Boolean conditions using logical operators.
Use truth tables to trace the results.

title: Combining Conditions
paragraphs: A logical operator combines Boolean conditions into one expression.
The and operator requires every condition to be True.
The or operator requires at least one condition to be True.
The combined result can be used as the condition in an if statement.

title: Truth Tables
paragraphs: A truth table shows every combination of Boolean inputs.
Each row shows the result for one combination.

title: The and Operator
paragraphs: The and operator gives True when both conditions are True.
Here, has_ticket and has_id are both True. The entry message is displayed.
Change either value to False to try the other branch.

title: The or Operator
paragraphs: The or operator gives True when at least one condition is True.
Here, is_holiday is True. The first message is displayed.
The result is False only when both conditions are False.

title: Grouping Conditions with Parentheses
paragraphs: Parentheses show how conditions are grouped.
The grouped expression has_ticket and has_pass is False.
The is_staff value is True. The or expression gives True. Access is granted.
code:
has_ticket = False
has_pass = True
is_staff = True

if (has_ticket and has_pass) or is_staff:
    print("Access granted.")
else:
    print("Access denied.")

title: Changing the Grouping
paragraphs: Here, has_pass or is_staff is grouped together. That group is True.
The outer and also requires has_ticket to be True.
Here, has_ticket is False. Access is denied.
code:
has_ticket = False
has_pass = True
is_staff = True

if has_ticket and (has_pass or is_staff):
    print("Access granted.")
else:
    print("Access denied.")

title: Checking a Number Between Values
paragraphs: The condition 0 < x < 10 checks an open range.
The value must be greater than 0. The value must also be less than 10.
The values 0 and 10 are excluded. Here, x is 5. Each check displays Valid.
code:
x = 5

# Using and
if x > 0 and x < 10:
    print("Valid")

# Chained comparison
if 0 < x < 10:
    print("Valid")

title: Wrap Up
bullets: Use and when every Boolean condition must be True.
Use or when at least one Boolean condition must be True.
Use a truth table to check each combination of inputs.
Use parentheses to make condition grouping clear.
Use 0 < x < 10 to check an open range. The endpoints are excluded.
